chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Sufyan ibn al-Samt, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

key_terms.الدُّهْنُ: Oil, unguent, or the act of anointing/massaging with oil
key_terms.السُّوءِ: Evil, harm, or illness (often referring to physical ailments in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical benefit of oiling or massaging according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the therapeutic efficacy of oiling (al-duhn), linking it to the removal of 'evil' (al-su'), which Shia scholars interpret broadly as physical ailments, bodily discomfort, or even minor spiritual impurities. This narration underscores the Islamic emphasis on preventive healthcare and the holistic view of the body, where simple physical care is seen as a means to restore balance and well-being.

en.hubeali:
